page: Amazon Web Services x8i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server instance featuring dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. The system is built on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 3072.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The processor features a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU and memory performance. While single-core stress-ng performance falls within the average tier, multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores rank in the top 10% globally. Memory bandwidth is highly optimized, with read-only operations for both small and large blocks achieving top-tier throughput, and large block write operations ranking in the top 25%. The platform also excels in database operations, with Passmark database tests and Redis SET operations both placing in the top 10% of benchmarked systems.

The instance includes a 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth but lacks local NVMe storage, requiring external network-attached storage for persistent data. This hardware profile offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for massive, memory-bound workloads that do not require local disk storage. The presence of AMX instructions enables strong performance in CPU-based LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing across small, medium, and large models. The server is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, heavy multi-threaded data processing, software compilation, and enterprise-grade virtualization.
